judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2) under Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations, so direction rests on statement content, not rank. The second SFI (B6.1.2.1.2) asks learners to apply mental mathematics strategies for multiplication — annexing then adding zero, halving and doubling, and the distributive property — under a Content Standard about basic multiplication facts to 144 and related division facts; its Learning Components isolate each of these strategies. The first SFI (B6.1.2.2.1) requires multiplying multi-digit numbers by 2 or 3-digit numbers 'efficiently', under a Content Standard on multiplication of 2/3-digit by 2/3-digit numbers. Fluency with the distributive property, annexing zeros, and doubling/halving is exactly what supports efficient multi-digit multiplication of larger factors, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first; the change is from strategy/fact-level mental methods to their application on larger multi-digit computations. Same-grade, same-sub-strand placement and shared 'multiplication' LC tagging corroborate substantive coherence rather than mere wording overlap.

The remaining nomination signals are non-semantic (shared Grade/Strand ancestors, weak rank proximity at gap 0, weak 'b4'/'1' code prefix, stopword token overlap 'and'/'the', morphological trigrams) and cannot supply direction.
